name: Watershed
title: Enterprise signals with evidence and a buying map
subtitle: Account intelligence · Seller workflows · Revenue systems
focus: Connect sustainability-related account context to the right stakeholders, seller action and a dependable commercial handoff.
priorities: Build an outbound signal engine and AI-assisted account intelligence.
Improve Salesforce, routing and CPQ workflows.
Work with GTM teams to turn requests into adopted systems.
Measure business impact and improve the operating process.
layers: Public company disclosures, business changes and source timestamps.
Sustainability, Finance, Operations and procurement roles with verified affiliations.
Existing account ownership, a relevant reason to engage and seller feedback.
Solution validation and CPQ dependencies, with adoption and business impact measured.
rules: A reporting mention is a research signal, not a legal conclusion about an obligation.
Verify stakeholder names and remit; a title alone does not prove buying authority.
Preserve commercial approval dependencies before a quote or commitment.

personas.name: Sustainability leader
personas.pain: Fragmented sustainability data and unclear ownership across teams
personas.promise: A discussion grounded in the published program and the current data process.
personas.subject: The data work behind {{initiative}}
personas.email: Hi {{first_name}}, your published {{initiative}} raises a practical question about how information moves across teams. How does your group collect, review and use that data today, and where does coordination slow down?
personas.question: Which teams produce the data, and who owns the review process?

personas.name: Finance / procurement leader
personas.pain: Cross-functional data needs and an enterprise approval process
personas.promise: A clear stakeholder map and an agreed scope for evaluating the workflow.
personas.subject: Connecting {{initiative}} to the operating process
personas.email: Hi {{first_name}}, I’m researching the operating process around {{initiative}}, including the Finance and procurement handoffs. Who should help define the data scope and evaluation criteria before a broader platform discussion?
personas.question: What needs to be true for a solution scope to enter commercial approval?

pitch: I have led technical enterprise sales across engineering, product, legal and customer stakeholders, and built source-backed data and CRM workflows myself. At Watershed, I would connect that commercial experience to verified account intelligence, buying-committee context and reliable revenue-system handoffs that sellers actually use.
mappings: BeBop technical sales through validation, proposals and negotiation.
Map stakeholders and commercial dependencies around a useful evaluation.
Hey Sammy: source-backed collection, structured records and validation.
Keep disclosure evidence and a clear hypothesis attached to the account.
Local partnership CRM and product analytics.
Deliver context in the seller workflow and measure usefulness.
northStar: Evidence-led seller action and dependable commercial handoffs
weekOne: A source-linked account brief and buying map for one enterprise segment.
days60: Expand ownership and stakeholder intelligence; measure adoption and fix a specific Salesforce or CPQ handoff.
days90: Connect accepted signals and commercial dependencies to business outcomes; scale workflows with observed seller value.
